haiku-low.q1: MySQL commits the write and its outbox row in one transaction first, then makes one best-effort copy to Postgres. A Postgres failure is swallowed and the request still succeeds.
haiku-low.q2: Only when the incoming version is higher than the stored row's version. A copy may also insert a missing row, and a tombstone guard blocks ids that were erased.
haiku-low.q3: Every web and worker process must export users.dual_write=true, with no old-build processes, then wait 2 more minutes. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds after a flag change.
haiku-low.q4: Before every batch it checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds. If lag is above 5 or missing, it sleeps 10 seconds and rechecks. Each read is capped at 1,000 rows.
haiku-low.q5: Reads: step 6 must report 0 mismatches, then the read percentage ramps 1, 10, 50, 100. Switch: 3+ days at 100% reads, latest comparison at 0, outbox idle, reverse paths tested.
haiku-low.q6: The outbox row, in the source-of-truth database and committed with the write, records that Postgres is behind. The drainer retries the copy with backoff, up to 60 seconds, until correct.
haiku-low.q7: Deletes insert a tombstone and delete the row in one transaction. Every copy statement has a NOT EXISTS tombstone guard, and MySQL never reuses ids, so erased users cannot return.
haiku-low.q8: Progress is backfill_state.last_id in Postgres, updated in the same transaction as each batch. The runner stops when a read returns no rows.
haiku-low.q9: The full comparison job walks both tables in id order. It rechecks each difference, heals it with an outbox row, and for extra Postgres ids the drainer writes a tombstone and deletes the row. Equal versions with different content page a human.
haiku-low.q10: Closing the MySQL fence makes every SoT write return 503, and the fence is checked in the database, not by flags. If the switch passes the 45-second deadline, MySQL is reopened. A watchdog reopens it after 60 seconds if the script crashes.
haiku-low.q11: Postgres's identity column assigns new ids after the switch. Its sequence is set past the max id in both databases plus 1000. Rollback sets MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to max(id)+1000 before reopening the MySQL fence.
haiku-low.q12: Reverse mirroring keeps MySQL current. Rollback closes the Postgres fence, drains its outbox, sets AUTO_INCREMENT, opens the MySQL fence and sets sot=mysql. It ends at step 11, when mirror becomes deletes_only.

sonnet.q1: MySQL (SoT) commits first, with an outbox row in the same transaction; then after commit one best-effort copy goes to Postgres. If the Postgres copy fails, the error is swallowed and the caller sees success.
sonnet.q2: Only if no row exists, or the existing row's version is lower than the incoming version (and the id has no tombstone). Otherwise it is skipped.
sonnet.q3: Every running process (web and workers) must show app_flag_value{flag="users.dual_write"}=true (series count equals process count), then wait a further 2 minutes; only then set backfill_enabled=true. Instances can disagree for up to 30 seconds (flag cache refresh interval).
sonnet.q4: Batches of at most 1,000 rows read from the MySQL replica (not primary), and before every batch it checks mysql_replica_lag_seconds: if above 5 or missing, it sleeps 10 seconds and rechecks (fails closed). A single runner holds a lease.
sonnet.q5: Reads: backfill finished, one full comparison pass reports 0 mismatches (and the outbox's oldest row is under 5 seconds), then ramp 1/10/50/100% while p99 latency and errors are healthy. SoT switch: at least 3 days at 100% reads, latest comparison 0 mismatches, outbox idle, and reverse-direction code paths (Postgres outbox, MySQL tombstones, fences) tested.
sonnet.q6: The outbox row (users_sync_outbox) inserted in the same MySQL transaction as the write, kept in the SoT (MySQL) database. The drainer worker re-reads the current row from the MySQL primary and copies it to Postgres with the version rule, retrying forever, then deletes the outbox rows.
sonnet.q7: Tombstones in users_erased (in both databases): deleting inserts the tombstone and deletes the row in one transaction, and every copy statement has a NOT EXISTS (tombstone) guard, so backfill, dual-write and repair copies skip erased ids. Ids are never reused by MySQL.
sonnet.q8: In Postgres backfill_state.last_id (with a lease row). It is updated (WHERE last_id < max id read) in the same Postgres transaction as the batch upsert, so it commits atomically with the copied rows. It stops when a read (id > last_id ORDER BY id from the replica) returns no rows.
sonnet.q9: The full comparison job walks both tables in id order and classifies each id as missing in Postgres, extra in Postgres, or different. It rechecks against the MySQL primary and outbox; a persisting difference with no pending outbox row is a mismatch, healed by inserting an outbox row (for extras, the drainer writes a tombstone and deletes the row). Any mismatch means the pass fails; rerun until 0. Equal version with different content pages a human.
sonnet.q10: The fence: the switcher closes the MySQL fence (waiting for in-flight writes via exclusive lock), so all SoT writes get a retryable 503 regardless of cached flags; Postgres fence opens only after drain and sequence set, then flags are set. Stale-flag instances hit the closed MySQL fence and 503 until they refresh (within 30s). If it runs long (45-second deadline for sub-steps 2-4 passes): reopen the MySQL fence, a clean abort; a watchdog reopens it after 60s if the script crashes before the Postgres fence opens. Worst case pause 75s, under the 90s limit.
sonnet.q11: Postgres, via an identity column GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY. At the switch the sequence is set to greatest(MySQL max(id) from primary, Postgres max(id)) + 1000. On rollback, MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT is set to max(id) + 1000.
sonnet.q12: With users.mirror=both the reverse mirror (Postgres outbox, quick copy, drainer, tombstones) keeps MySQL current; daily two-way comparison during a 14-day soak. Rollback is the switch in reverse: close the Postgres fence, drain the Postgres outbox to zero, set MySQL AUTO_INCREMENT to max(id)+1000, open the MySQL fence, set users.sot=mysql and mirror=both (45s deadline, 75s worst case). The option ends at step 11 when users.mirror is set to deletes_only (point of no return, requires 14+ days since the switch, empty outbox, final comparison 0).
